races.name: Army Benevolent Fund/ebf Novice Stakes (gbb Race)
Hugh James Classified Stakes

runners_data.name: Iconic Times
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with no wins or placed finishes on similar going (0W0P in 2/15 runs on standard going), returning quickly on just 5 days' rest for Jennie Candlish; all five recent runs over 6-8f on standard tracks have produced double-figure finishes and there is very little here to suggest a revival.
runners_data.comment: Iconic Times bounced back to winning ways last time out and, drawn in stall two carrying 140 lb, he has experience of both today's trip and going. Our rating of 65 makes him the one to beat, though the quick five-day turnaround is worth noting.

runners_data.name: Due Respect
runners_data.note: Gary Rutherford's runner has placed twice on good ground in 15 similar-going starts, and while his best form is over this 7f trip, he is a natural deep closer who is squeezed into a midfield role here by the volume of hold-up horses — his chance depends on the shape creating a genuine late opportunity that this race is unlikely to provide.
runners_data.comment: Due Respect has been ninth last time out and eighth two starts back, and her recent sequence offers little encouragement; yet to win in her last six starts and ranked sixth of seven on our figures, she faces a stiff ask here despite experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Rain Cap
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old with genuine good-ground credentials (1W5P in 9/15 similar-going starts) and consistent placed efforts over today's 7f trip; Ethan Tindall rides off a 5lb claim which helps at the weights, and this is arguably the most straightforward profile in the field to slot behind the leader and stay on.
runners_data.comment: Rain Cap has run over today's trip and going, and at just nine days between starts he arrives in sharp order — his earlier third and second show he can get competitive when in the mood. The worry is that he's been winless in his last six, and that latest seventh suggests he can also disappoint.

runners_data.name: Wait For It
runners_data.note: Billy Garritty partners a horse with three placed efforts on good ground over 6-7f including a second and a third at this trip — a genuine hold-up horse by nature who will end up racing in midfield rather than off the pace, which tempers how strongly he can produce his best finishing effort; 4 days since last run is quick but not alarming.
runners_data.comment: Consistent front-runner profile makes Wait For It a genuine threat — third last time out, and second two starts back, she has experience over today's trip and going, and our rating has her well ahead of her official mark. The concern is that she runs just four days on.

runners_data.name: Without Delay
runners_data.note: Tracy Waggott's seven-year-old has placed three times on good ground and won once in 12 similar-going starts, but has been running in longer-distance races (8-9f) recently and drops back to 7f here; like several others he is a natural backmarker shuffled into a midfield role, and 19 days since last run is straightforward.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, Without Delay does bring distance and going experience to the table, and 19 days since her last run leaves her reasonably fresh; however, her recent string of unplaced efforts makes it hard to fancy her reversing that trend from stall one off 135 lb.

runners_data.name: Ziva's Star
runners_data.note: Andrew Elliott rides a four-year-old whose recent form includes a third at 5f on good ground but who has been racing over sprint trips rather than today's 7f, raising a stamina-suitability question; held up by preference but unable to get that position in this race, she faces the compound challenge of an unsuited race shape and an unproven trip.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts and ranked last on our figures, Ziva's Star faces a stiff task here; the one bright spot is a third three starts back, and she has experience over today's trip and going, returning fit after 21 days off.

runners_data.name: Our Hero Matty
runners_data.note: The only confirmed prominent/front-running type in the field, trained by Tony Culhane & Stella Barclay and ridden by Barry McHugh; stepping up markedly in trip from his 5-6f runs and today's 7f is a query, but his role as uncontested leader means he controls the pace and can dictate his own energy expenditure — the trip question is the chief reservation against him holding on.
runners_data.comment: Placed third two starts back and returning on a sound 21-day break, Our Hero Matty has run over today's trip and going and rates above his official mark — the risk is that he's winless in his last five starts.

races.paceDynamic: Our Hero Matty is the sole confirmed front-runner in this seven-runner field and, with no genuine challenger to his early position, he should stride into an uncontested lead from the outset and control a sustainable gallop around Catterick's flat seven furlongs. The pace he sets is unlikely to be a searching one — a lone leader without pressure can afford to roll along at a measured tempo, conserving energy and making the race difficult to unpick from behind. Due Respect, Wait For It, Without Delay, and Ziva's Star are all genuine hold-up horses by inclination but this field contains more deep closers than the race shape can accommodate at the rear, meaning several of those four will end up racing in a midfield cluster rather than their preferred off-the-pace berth. This race shape strongly favours a prominent or front-running profile: a single uncontested leader on good ground over seven furlongs at Catterick is a textbook scenario where the horse on the front end dictates and holds on, with only a genuine, well-positioned midfield tracker possessing the class and timing to reel him in.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Our Hero Matty is allowed to stride clear and regulate a comfortable pace without sustained early pressure.
scenarios.body: Our Hero Matty dictates from flag to finish on this flat track, using the lack of a challenger to conserve enough energy to hold off all comers in the straight; good ground suits his profile and Catterick's seven furlongs has no demanding topography to force him back.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Midfield Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just strong enough that a well-positioned midfield horse times a late run to collar a tiring leader.
scenarios.body: Rain Cap, with solid form on good ground over seven furlongs and a genuine ability to finish races off a genuine pace, is ideally placed to benefit if Our Hero Matty goes too fast too soon; at nine years old Rain Cap is experienced enough to judge the race and a 1W5P record on similar going gives him honest claims.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the final furlong and a closers' finish develops at the rear of the field.
scenarios.body: Due Respect or Without Delay would need a genuine, pressured pace to close onto, but both are mapped away from their natural ground-covering hold-up role and must race further forward than ideal; their style-fit concerns are real, and without a collapsing leader this shape is unlikely to materialise.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Muddle
scenarios.trigger: If Our Hero Matty stops abruptly and the race becomes a ragged sprint finish among a bunched field.
scenarios.body: In a messy scramble any horse in the right place at the right time could benefit, but Iconic Times — a hold-up type with modest recent form — and Ziva's Star offer low-probability each-way interest purely on chaos value; this scenario requires multiple things to go wrong simultaneously and is assigned minimal weight.

watchPoints.text: Our Hero Matty's stamina over 7f is unproven — all five recent runs have been over 5-6f, and if he ties up in the final furlong having gone too freely in front the race opens up dramatically for the closers.

Rain Cap's jockey Ethan Tindall claims 5lb, giving him a significant weight advantage; if Rain Cap tracks the leader in second or third, watch whether Tindall can time the challenge to catch a tiring Our Hero Matty in the final 100 yards.

The cluster of redistributed hold-up horses — Due Respect, Wait For It, Without Delay, Ziva's Star — will be racing further forward than ideal; if they jostle for midfield positions in the early stages it could create minor interference or unsettled runs without generating any extra pace pressure on the leader.

Catterick's seven-furlong track is flat and straight, which means there is no bend or downhill section to aid closers gaining momentum — late runs require a genuinely fading leader, making the hold-up profile even less favoured than usual here.

The going is confirmed Good for this race and has been consistent across all distances on the card; no horse carries a specific going concern, but Due Respect and Rain Cap have the most solid records on this surface among the hold-up types.

races.name: Jacky Rylance 60th Birthday Celebration Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Free World
runners_data.note: Confirmed hold-up type for Ian Williams, ridden by Cieren Fallon, but carries a fade-in-finish flag that is a serious concern in a likely slow-run race where the sprint finish will be sharp; 0W0P in six similar-going runs is a red flag despite reasonable recent form figures.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts, Free World at least returns on a reasonable freshness of 31 days and has experience of today's going; however, a fourth last time out masks a patchy recent record, and carrying 135 lb with our rating below the official mark are legitimate concerns.

runners_data.name: Karthala
runners_data.note: Sean Bowen takes over for Jennie Candlish, and the four-year-old has a strong placed record at this distance on Good ground — 5 placings from 15 similar-going efforts with strong 16f and 20f form suggest stamina is genuine; hood and tongue-tie combination worth noting, and 20 days since last run is a fresh enough preparation.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Karthala does bring some encouragement — fifth two starts back and a second five starts back suggest he retains ability, and he arrives fit at 20 days since his last run with going experience in his favour, despite a hefty 135 lb to carry.

runners_data.name: Fleur de Mer
runners_data.note: Martin Todhunter's six-year-old wears a visor and has limited Good-ground form (2/15 sim-going), spending most of her recent starts on Soft or Standard, which makes the current surface a mild query; placed at 14f and 12f recently, and a hold-up horse who will need the sprint finish to arrive cleanly.
runners_data.comment: Fleur de Mer arrives here as our top-rated runner on adjusted figures, and her third three starts back and runner-up four starts back highlight a consistent knack for hitting the frame — she has run over today's trip and going, and 26 days off the track suggests she arrives fresh. The risk is that she has been winless in her last five starts and must prove she can convert.

runners_data.name: Zephlyn
runners_data.note: Despite being a true hold-up horse by inclination, Jason Hart's mount is the only realistic pace-setter here and has been mapped to the front by necessity — the STYLE_FIT discount of 0.80 is meaningful, and his 52-day absence adds a fitness query; two wins from seven on similar going show he handles the surface, but racing against his nature over 2m is a significant ask.
runners_data.comment: Zephlyn shaped with promise when third three starts back and has experience of today's trip and conditions, making him a genuine threat at a big weight of 131 lb — though he's been winless in his last five starts and must find more consistency.

runners_data.name: Slack Alice
runners_data.note: Luke Morris rides for Mickey Bowen, and this five-year-old has genuine stamina credentials — two wins at 22f and 23f on Good ground stand out as the best distance form in the field; a true hold-up horse shown in midfield only because the rear is overcrowded, and the STYLE_FIT of 0.92 means the map position barely changes her tactical outlook.
runners_data.comment: Consistent without a win in her last five starts, Slack Alice nevertheless brings solid placed form — third last time out — and has run over today's trip and going; the worry is she must find improvement to justify a rating of 63 against this field.

runners_data.name: Speechman
runners_data.note: Cam Hardie partners Philip Kirby's six-year-old just four days after its last run — quick turnaround for a horse carrying a fade-in-finish warning and tongue-bar headgear; a natural hold-up horse placed in midfield on the map through redistribution, and the 0W2P record on similar going alongside the short recovery period tempers enthusiasm.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and ranked seventh of nine on our figures, Speechman has precious little to recommend him here despite returning quickly four days ago; he has run over today's trip and going, but a seventh last time out makes it hard to be enthusiastic.

runners_data.name: Lillistar
runners_data.note: Micky Hammond's six-year-old returns 16 days after last time out wearing a hood, and has placed four times from seven on Good ground at this sort of trip; a true hold-up type whose map midfield position is a product of field congestion rather than style — consistent without winning, and will need a well-run race to produce her best.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Lillistar has shown some resilience — placed third last time out and third two starts back — but a 1lb deficit to her official rating and an eighth-of-nine ranking on our figures make her hard to fancy despite having run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Star Of Jupiter
runners_data.note: Mark Loughnane's five-year-old, partnered by William Pyle, has shown promise at 14f with a second on Good ground and wears tongue-tie and blinkers; a 40-day break and a hold-up style mapped to midfield by necessity mean he needs things to go his way, and the 0W3P similar-going record suggests a horse that finds one too good.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Star Of Jupiter at least has experience over today's trip and going to call on, and a run 40 days ago leaves him acceptably fresh — though his official mark of 45 and mid-pack ranking suggest he faces a stiff task against stronger rivals here.

runners_data.name: Ruler Of The River
runners_data.note: Barry McHugh rides Philip Kirby's second string, with headgear of hood and tongue-tie, last seen only seven days ago and with form figures that include a couple of unknowns over big distances; the 1W3P record on similar going is the best strike rate in the field on that measure, and if this genuinely stays 2m he could be an each-way player, though a true hold-up horse racing out of natural position on the map.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts, with a string of unplaced efforts before a fifth and sixth in more recent outings, Ruler Of The River faces a stiff task ranked last on our figures; at least today's distance and going hold no secrets for her.

races.paceDynamic: Zephlyn is the sole confirmed pace-setter here, redistributed to the front from a true hold-up profile, meaning this 2m trip at Catterick will be run at a genuinely sustainable, uncontested tempo with no horse likely to push him hard early. Behind him, the entire remainder of the field is made up of hold-up types, with Slack Alice, Speechman, Lillistar, Star Of Jupiter, and Ruler Of The River all redistributed to midfield simply because the map cannot accommodate nine closers — in reality this race shapes as a near-wall-to-wall hold-up field chasing a single reluctant pace-setter. The field holds more hold-up and midfield types than can realistically get their natural position; Zephlyn is most likely to set the tempo, but with no genuine frontrunner pressing him, the pace is likely to be modest and the race will bunch up before a late sprint for home over Catterick's straight finish. This shape overwhelmingly favours horses with a strong finishing kick who can travel comfortably in a slowly-run race and accelerate when the tempo finally lifts — hold-up horses with good recent form on Good ground and proven stamina at the trip are best placed.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Slow Burn, Late Sprint
scenarios.trigger: If Zephlyn sets a modest uncontested gallop and the field crawls into the straight before a mass sprint finish.
scenarios.body: Zephlyn dictates on easy terms with no rival willing to take him on, compressing the entire field into a tight bunch before a furious dash from two furlongs out; horses with a sharp finishing kick over this sort of trip on Good ground will be at a premium.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Picks Up Midrace
scenarios.trigger: If one of the redistributed midfield horses — most likely Slack Alice or Lillistar — pushes forward to challenge Zephlyn and injects a more genuine gallop from halfway.
scenarios.body: A truer test of stamina develops, stringing the field out and suiting the horses who have proven themselves over 2m-plus on Good ground with strong finishing form; real stayers rather than quick-finishing types come to the fore.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Outstays Field
scenarios.trigger: If Zephlyn, despite racing out of role, settles beautifully on a lone lead and builds enough advantage in the straight that chasers cannot close.
scenarios.body: With a lenient gallop entirely under his own control, Zephlyn could exploit his position and the inability of true hold-up horses to quicken from too far back; his STYLE_FIT of 0.80 tempers confidence but the scenario is possible if connections have deliberately placed him here.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers All Fail to Fire
scenarios.trigger: If the modest pace lures too many horses wide or into traffic trouble in the home straight, causing a messy finish where no hold-up horse gets a clean run.
scenarios.body: Disorganisation in a bunched field sees form horses fail to produce their finishing effort, handing an opportunity to any horse that has tracked closer throughout; horses with recent course-and-distance experience and reliable headgear score.

watchPoints.text: Zephlyn is racing entirely against his natural hold-up style as the lone pace-setter — watch whether Jason Hart actually elects to go forward at the start or allows another horse to take up the running, which would leave the race with no true front-runner at all.

Slack Alice and Lillistar are both genuine hold-up horses crowded into a midfield map position — if they push forward to get cover early, they risk overracing and compromising their finishing effort in what is likely to be a sprint-home scenario.

Speechman's four-day turnaround and fade-in-finish flag combine as a notable concern — watch for signs of a sluggish or reluctant start from Cam Hardie's mount that could confirm the quick return is taking its toll.

With nine hold-up types contesting a 2m race at Catterick, traffic and positioning in the home straight could be decisive — watch for horses widest on the track or with the cleanest passage from two furlongs out, as a bunched finish is the most likely outcome.

Karthala's strong placed record at 16f and 20f on Good ground makes him the best-credentialled stayer in the field on sim-going evidence — watch whether Sean Bowen positions him to travel smoothly behind the pace rather than getting caught in the midfield scrimmage.

races.name: Hannah Blanchard 21st Birthday Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Captain Cess
runners_data.note: Won over 7f good ground 19 days ago in strong form (form: 231 recent), handles 6f well with a second at the trip on soft; natural hold-up runner arriving with momentum and a capable handler in Declan Carroll, though his best form has come slightly further.|
runners_data.comment: Captain Cess arrives on the back of a win last time out and has run over today's trip and going, yet he carries 138 lb from stall 2 and his speed rating of 54 suggests he may need to find more to confirm that recent improvement.

runners_data.name: Miss Rainbow
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed pace-setter wearing a visor, Connor Beasley takes the ride, with 10 runs on similar going producing two wins and seven places — she is ideally set up to dictate on a flat 6f Catterick track, and an 11-day turnaround looks sharp but manageable.|
runners_data.comment: Miss Rainbow brings strong recent form — third two starts back and third three starts back — and has run over today's trip and going, while 11 days ago keeps her fresh; the worry is that fourth last time out suggests she just held form, and 137 lb is a stern burden to overcome.

runners_data.name: Barmyblade
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby sends out a horse with four wins on good ground from 13 attempts, a genuine hold-up horse by nature though placed in midfield here because true closers outnumber available rear slots; Sean Kirrane on board, and the horse's best efforts have come when getting a proper end to run at — a moderate pace blunts that.|
runners_data.comment: Barmyblade won last time out and has experience of today's trip and conditions, but a cold trainer strike-rate of just 3% over the past fortnight is a notable concern for a gelding rated 57 heading out from stall 8.

runners_data.name: Lucius Aurelius
runners_data.note: Kevin Ryan's prominent-going type has a pedestrian recent record at 5f but steps back to 6f where his sole win came on good ground; the 3lb claim of Jack Nicholls adds value, though recent form figures of 0-1-0-3-8-9 suggest he needs things to fall kindly.|
runners_data.comment: Lucius Aurelius ran third three starts back and struck in the fifth start listed, giving him a mix of promise and patchy recent form; he has run over today's distance and going, arrives fresh on 20 days' rest, and our rating of 63 puts him second of the eight, though the 136 lb burden is the obvious risk.

runners_data.name: Howzak
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old hold-up horse whose similar-going record reads just 2 placed from 15, with no wins on ground like this; Billy Garritty partners, but Howzak's best recent form has come on standard artificial surfaces and this flat turf good-ground test looks a genuine concern.|
runners_data.comment: Howzak has been beaten out of the first four in three straight starts and, ranked last on our figures, makes no appeal at the weights. He has run over today's trip and going, and the 13-day turnaround suggests he's fit, but that's the limit of the case for him.

runners_data.name: Call Glory
runners_data.note: Ian Williams' runner is a consistent placer at 7f on good ground (four placed from six) but steps back to 6f and races at a shorter trip than his optimum; a genuine closer by style, pushed into a midfield slot by field congestion, and without a win in 15 runs on comparable going this remains a concern.|
runners_data.comment: Call Glory has been a model of consistency, finishing second twice in his last three starts, and he has experience of today's trip and conditions. Yet to score in recent starts, but drawn six carrying 135 lb, his rating of 64 marks him as the one to beat here.

runners_data.name: Enjoy The Night
runners_data.note: Three-year-old trained by Seb Spencer, a natural hold-up horse who has been placed twice at 5f-8f on good ground but carries the style-fit discount of racing out of position; at OR=56 there is some upside, but finishing positions of 5-9-7-5-3 underline that finding the front end is not straightforward.|
runners_data.comment: Enjoy The Night showed his best in recent starts when third last time out, and he has experience of today's trip and conditions — the main concern is that he's been winless in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Battenburg Belle
runners_data.note: Rebecca Menzies' lightly-weighted three-year-old has been placed in five of six starts including a win at 6f on good ground, making her form profile arguably the most consistent in the field; a true hold-up horse shuffled into midfield by congestion, Jason Hart takes the ride and the OR=51 mark could see her sneaking an each-way position if the pace collapses.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked seventh of eight on our figures, Battenburg Belle is hard to fancy at the head of affairs, though she does arrive fit on a nine-day turnaround, has run over today's trip and going, and showed she can win when taking a race three starts back. Fifth two starts back is the concern.

races.paceDynamic: Miss Rainbow is the sole confirmed front-runner and will lead from the outset under Connor Beasley, setting a sustainable gallop on good ground over 6f at Catterick — a track that rewards horses who travel kindly and don't burn excess energy early. With no other natural pace-setter to pressure her, she is expected to control tempo from the front without being harried, creating a single-file, steady-to-honest gallop that makes it genuinely difficult for pure hold-up horses to generate enough momentum off a false pace. The field is heavily weighted toward hold-up types — Barmyblade, Call Glory, Enjoy The Night and Battenburg Belle are all genuine closers who have been redistributed to midfield on the map simply because the rear is overcrowded, meaning they are unlikely to race in their natural position and their late-running threat is structurally compromised. This shape — one uncontested leader, a compressed midfield of hold-up horses racing out of role, and a good, consistent surface — strongly favours front-running and prominent-racing profiles to dominate from the front and simply not be caught.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Miss Rainbow Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Miss Rainbow is allowed to stride clear unchallenged and sets a measured, rail-hugging gallop on good ground.
scenarios.body: She dictates every fraction, conserves energy through the bend, and kicks again entering the final furlong before the closers — racing out of their natural positions — can organise a meaningful challenge. Front-running and prominent profiles suit entirely, and her good-ground record of 10/15 confirms she is built for exactly these conditions.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Strikes Late
scenarios.trigger: If Miss Rainbow's pace proves just strong enough to bring Lucius Aurelius and Captain Cess into the race late without flattering the true hold-up types.
scenarios.body: Lucius Aurelius, racing prominently off the pace, tracks the leader through the bend and uses his sprint pedigree to pounce inside the final furlong on ground he handles well enough. Captain Cess, fresh off a win 19 days ago with strong 6f good-ground form, arrives with a sustained run from midfield to threaten.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Overturn Pace
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace proves faster than expected and Miss Rainbow ties up inside the final furlong, leaving a gap for the redistributed hold-up horses.
scenarios.body: Barmyblade, with four wins on good ground in 13 runs and course-suitable form, is the most credible of the hold-up contingent to exploit such a collapse, while Battenburg Belle's consistent placed form and 6f good-ground record give her an each-way claim. This scenario requires multiple things to go right simultaneously and is structurally unlikely given the redistribution of the hold-up group.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Low-Key Upset
scenarios.trigger: If the race is run at a muddling tempo that scrambles the field and elevates a lightly-weighted or unexposed runner.
scenarios.body: Battenburg Belle at OR=51 carries the lightest weight and has shown a knack for placing consistently in good-ground 6f handicaps; a bunched, messy finish could see her sneak into a frame position. Enjoy The Night, younger and potentially underrated on an easing handicap mark, is the longer-shot beneficiary if the shape turns chaotic.

watchPoints.text: Miss Rainbow — if she bowls along uncontested at the front under Connor Beasley and clears entering the final 2f, the hold-up horses racing out of position have almost no mechanism to reel her in on this flat 6f track.

Barmyblade and Battenburg Belle — both genuine closers forced into midfield roles; watch their positioning at halfway, because if they are stuck behind a wall of horses who have also moved forward, they will have no clear run to deliver their finishing effort.

Lucius Aurelius — if he pushes forward early to claim a prominent position, he could become the key rival to Miss Rainbow, but his 5f-heavy recent campaign raises a stamina question as the race develops into the final furlong.

Howzak — eight-year-old hold-up type with zero wins or places on good turf in 15 attempts at similar going; market move without obvious justification in the data would be a red flag worth noting before the off.

Captain Cess — last-run winner over 7f on good ground just 19 days ago; if he travels smoothly through midfield rather than getting blocked behind the redistributed hold-up cluster, he is the most likely danger to the front pair in the straight.

races.name: Racingtv.com Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Brunello Breeze
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up horse who has not run for 146 days and carries a headgear flag (hg:p); his simulation-going record is a modest 0 wins 1 place from 15 starts in similar conditions, and the fade-in-finish tag compounds the concern about a long layoff into a competitive handicap.
runners_data.comment: Brunello Breeze has run over today's trip and going, and our rating ranks him highest in this field — yet winless in his last five starts and returning after 146 days, the fitness query looms as the key risk to go with his uninspiring recent figures.

runners_data.name: On The Bubble
runners_data.note: Recent winner on Good ground at 1m4f (2nd in last visit, 0W6P in sim-going) with Clifford Lee, a strong booking; though a natural hold-up type, the congestion at the rear means he is likely to race closer than ideal, which tempers confidence despite 12 similar-going appearances offering solid experience.
runners_data.comment: Yet to score in her last six starts, On The Bubble does bring distance and going experience to the table, and a return just 15 days ago suggests she's fit — but a recent unplaced effort and modest official rating of 50 leave plenty to prove at this level.

runners_data.name: Halimede
runners_data.note: Sir Mark Prescott's three-year-old has run three times at 8f on Standard, so today's step up to 1m4f on Good turf is entirely uncharted territory; the fade-in-finish flag and limited form string (988) give little encouragement that he will improve with this extra distance.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts — all eighths or a ninth — Halimede arrives after a 47-day break and our rating of 48 suggests she faces a stiff ask against this field, though a trainer firing at 32% over the past fortnight offers a sliver of hope.

runners_data.name: Hansteen
runners_data.note: The race's only front-runner, he won over 1m4f on Good and placed twice over the same trip, giving him clear course-and-distance relevance; Jason Hart's handling of a lone leader role will be key, and with just 12 days since his last run he arrives fresh enough to hold form.
runners_data.comment: Hansteen shaped with real promise when runner-up last time out, and a winner two starts back, he arrives in good heart just 12 days on. He has run over today's trip and going before, and a rating of 68 makes him our pick against a strong field.

runners_data.name: Muhib
runners_data.note: Warren Fentiman claims 3lb on a horse whose five most recent runs read 2-3-3-4-4, all at 1m4f to 1m6f on Good or Soft — relentless consistency without a win but always in the frame; his natural style pushes him back from his preferred position, yet his reliability makes him the most credible threat to Hansteen if the pace tells.
runners_data.comment: Muhib has been placed in four of his last six starts — second last time out, and thirds two and three starts back — giving him a strong claims case at a mark of 46, though he remains yet to win in recent starts and that habit of running into a placing rather than forcing the issue is the chief concern.

runners_data.name: Project Kinsman
runners_data.note: Philip Kirby's three-year-old has shown ability stepping up in trip (placed at 1m4f on Good) but his simulation-going record is thin (0W1P from 8 runs); a genuine hold-up horse, he will likely end up closer to the pace than suits him, and Cam Hardie will need to manage that displacement carefully.
runners_data.comment: Placed third last time out and third four starts back, Project Kinsman has shown she can hit the frame and has run over today's trip — the key risk is that, winless in her last six starts, she has yet to prove she can convert.

runners_data.name: N'Ion
runners_data.note: Ian Williams has been busy (5/40 in 14 days) but this three-year-old's recent form offers little — his best Good-ground run was a fifth, and the fade-in-finish tag alongside a single placing in five similar-going efforts (0W0P) marks him as a tail-ender in the probability order.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with a string of mid-field and tail-end finishes, N'Ion is hard to fancy on these figures — ranked seventh of eight — though he has run over today's trip before and returns on a handy 12-day turnaround.

runners_data.name: Spirit Of Tokyo
runners_data.note: The second Philip Kirby runner, Spirit Of Tokyo has run only on Good and Standard going but exclusively at shorter trips (7f-8f) until now, making this 1m4f assignment a significant question; 0 wins and 0 places from four similar-going starts, and Aiden Brookes takes the ride with little to build on.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts, with finishes of seventh, eighth and sixth offering little encouragement, Spirit Of Tokyo rates the outsider on our figures and faces a stiff task here; the light weight is the one tangible positive.

races.paceDynamic: Hansteen is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pace rival to push him, will stride into the lead from the off and control tempo on his own terms around Catterick's flat mile-and-a-half. The remainder of the field — On The Bubble, Muhib, Project Kinsman, N'Ion and Spirit Of Tokyo — are all natural hold-up horses redistributed into midfield on the map because there are simply too many rear-of-field types for them all to operate from their preferred position; in practice several will find themselves closer to the pace than they would choose. Brunello Breeze and Halimede fill the back positions but both carry fading-in-finish flags, limiting their threat from a patient ride. With Hansteen able to dictate an honest but uncontested gallop, this race shape overwhelmingly favours a stalking prominent racer who can track the leader and pounce in the straight, rather than a deep hold-up horse relying on a strong finishing burst that this steady, controlled tempo will not generate.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hansteen Controls Leads Home
scenarios.trigger: If Hansteen bowls along unchallenged, sets a sustainable pace and finds enough in the straight to hold every challenger.
scenarios.body: Jason Hart settles Hansteen in front at whatever fractions he chooses, and without any rival forcing him honest he can conserve energy for the final two furlongs; his recent 1m4f form on Good ground (1st and two seconds) shows he handles this exact scenario well. Front-runners are rarely headed when they have this level of control at Catterick's flat gallop, and at OR 58 he is well within his range.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closest Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Hansteen sets a genuine pace but ties up in the final furlong, allowing the horse tracking closest to sweep past.
scenarios.body: A horse who travels smoothly just off the leader's quarters throughout would be perfectly positioned as Hansteen's lead narrows and the finish approaches; this suits a horse willing to race closer than its natural preference on this occasion. Muhib has consistently filled the frame at 1m4f-1m6f on Good ground and his reliable consistency makes him the likeliest beneficiary if the pace is hot enough to find Hansteen out.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Threads Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely brisk and the field strings out, creating enough of a run for a late finisher to close ground.
scenarios.body: On The Bubble and Project Kinsman are genuine hold-up horses who, if they manage to secure a position closer to their natural style than the map suggests, could produce a late challenge on Good ground that suits their form profiles. However, this scenario is discounted because most redistibuted horses in this field are unlikely to get far enough back to generate the momentum needed, and Hansteen's likely controlled tempo will not create the gaps a closer needs.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Hansteen is pressured unexpectedly early or misses the break, triggering a contested, ragged gallop that scrambles the race.
scenarios.body: An untidy pace scenario would devalue positional advantage and theoretically give the deeper hold-up horses a chance via a strong late rally, but this is the least likely shape given the one-dimensional front-running dynamic and the absence of any confirmed rival to push Hansteen. Even in this shape the faders — Brunello Breeze and Halimede — would struggle to deliver.

watchPoints.text: Hansteen — if Jason Hart is uncontested through the early furlongs and posts slow sectionals, he could steal an unassailable lead before the field reacts; monitor whether any rider attempts to close the gap before the home turn.

Muhib — his five consecutive placed efforts at this trip on Good suggest he is knocking on the door of a win; if Warren Fentiman manages to sit just off Hansteen rather than being marooned further back, his consistency makes him a live danger late.

On The Bubble — Clifford Lee is a significant jockey booking for Gary Rutherford and this horse's recent 1m4f Good-ground form is relevant; the redistribution away from its preferred hold-up slot means watching where Lee actually positions him from the stalls.

Halimede — Luke Morris rides for Sir Mark Prescott, a trainer known for placing horses to peak at the right moment, but three runs over 8f on Standard with no Good-ground or 1m4f experience means trip and going are genuinely unknown quantities today.

Project Kinsman and Spirit Of Tokyo — two runners from the same Philip Kirby yard with a 0/13 trainer 14-day strike rate; worth noting whether either is here to set up the other tactically, though both carry redistributed-style flags that limit their direct winning chance.

races.name: Racing Again 17th August Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Without Flaw
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with strong Good-ground 5f form (11 of 15 sim-going runs placed or won), consistent Tina Jackson yard going 1/5 in the last 14 days, and fresh off just 7 days rest — a reliable each-way conveyance who should sit a handy second or third throughout.
runners_data.comment: Without Flaw heads our ratings with a speed figure of 60, and her experience over today's trip and going keeps her firmly in the mix off draw five — the main concern is that she's winless in recent starts, with a string of back-of-field finishes to overcome.

runners_data.name: Brain Freeze
runners_data.note: Headgear flagged (hg:v) and trained by the high-volume Michael Dods yard (5 wins from 30 in 14 days); has won and placed multiple times over 5f on Good going, giving it the strongest closer profile in the field if it can thread a path at the business end.
runners_data.comment:
Counting from latest-first: 1st=5th, 2nd=5th, 3rd=6th, 4th=3rd, 5th=1st, 6th=5th.

So the win was five starts back, and the placed finish (3rd) was four starts back.

Brain Freeze arrives on the back of consecutive fifth-place finishes but has experience over today's trip and going, and a win five starts back hints at ability; at 131

runners_data.name: Doralee
runners_data.note: Jason Hart takes the ride for the David & Nicola Barron yard who are winless in the past 14 days (0/8), but Doralee herself holds an excellent sim-going record (12/15) and her recent runner-up at this trip and going makes her a legitimate prominent threat despite the trainer dip.
runners_data.comment: Doralee shaped well when second last time out and has experience over today's trip and going, with our rating of 53 putting her in the mix; the risk is she has been winless in recent starts, and 129 lb from stall one will need managing.

runners_data.name: Havin A Flyer
runners_data.note: The race's only confirmed front-runner, handled by claimer Tom Kiely-Marshall (5lb claim), but critically all sim-going form reads 1/15 — the switch from Southwell's Tapeta to Good turf is an unproven surface change that could undermine her otherwise solid front-running credentials (headgear: t flagged).
runners_data.comment: Havin A Flyer was a winner two starts back and has been consistently placed in recent starts, finishing third last time out just five days ago. She has experience of today's trip and going, and 129 lb from stall seven is the key query.

runners_data.name: Gwen Tennyson
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly for the Gemma Tutty yard who has crept closer in recent runs (3rd, 4th, 6th latest) and shows 4/7 sim-going efforts, but 11 days between runs and a naturally deep racing style means she depends on the pace folding to reach her best work at the 5f trip.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, Gwen Tennyson does have experience of today's trip and going in her favour, but a deteriorating recent sequence — ninth last time out — and a modest official mark of 49 make progress hard to envisage from stall 2.

runners_data.name: Mimime
runners_data.note: Michael Appleby-trained three-year-old whose actual running style is a true hold-up finisher (fades in finish flagged), but the surplus of hold-up types in this field means she is placed in midfield on the map rather than at the rear where she genuinely wants to race — limited form base of three runs (all 6f) adds further uncertainty at 5f.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts — including an eighth and a seventh — Mimime has run over today's trip but her trainer's recent strike rate of just 1/29 makes it hard to build a case, and our rating has her as the lowest-ranked of the seven runners.

runners_data.name: Dunnington Lad
runners_data.note: Six-year-old for Peter Winks (0/1 in the last 14 days) who is a genuine hold-up operator at his best, yet the congested hold-up sector pushes him forward on the map away from his favoured deep position; his 12/15 sim-going record is the one redeeming data point, but racing out of role at a low OR of 45 limits the ceiling here.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, with a third two runs back the lone bright spot in a largely modest recent profile, Dunnington Lad faces a stiff ask here — though he has run over today's trip and going before, and returns quickly on just eight days' rest.

races.paceDynamic: Havin A Flyer is the sole confirmed front-runner and should stride directly into an uncontested lead on Catterick's sharp, turning 5f, dictating a sustainable gallop that suits a horse who has won and placed multiple times from the front at Southwell's equivalent pace-friendly conditions. Without Flaw and Doralee will press from prominent positions, creating a two-three-horse breakaway that controls the tempo without turning it into a true test of stamina. The hold-up contingent — Brain Freeze, Gwen Tennyson, Mimime, and Dunnington Lad — will be hunting from the rear on a tight, flat track where gaps can close but where a clear-travelling leader has a genuine edge. Note that this field holds more genuine hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate at the rear; Mimime and Dunnington Lad are mapped to midfield because they are unlikely to secure their natural deep position, and their effectiveness in this race is consequently reduced. The tactical verdict is clear: this race shape strongly favours prominent and front-running profiles — horses that can travel kindly in the first two furlongs and sustain their effort to the line without needing a prolonged final-furlong surge.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Leader Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Havin A Flyer jumps cleanly and none of the prominent types aggressively contest the early lead, leaving the pace uncontested through the first two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Havin A Flyer controls tempo from the front and, racing on Good ground for the first time having shown sim-going form only at Southwell, must prove the surface switch is not a concern — but the lack of pressure means its natural front-running rhythm is preserved regardless. Prominent types Without Flaw and Doralee sit in ideal stalking positions and are the primary beneficiaries if the leader ties up, given both carry strong Good-ground profiles and can pick up at the furlong pole.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If Havin A Flyer sets a pace fractionally too strong and the two prominent chasers Without Flaw and Doralee close strongly inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Without Flaw's consistent Good-ground form over 5f at Catterick-equivalent tracks and Doralee's recent runner-up effort at this trip and going give both the credentials to profit from a leader who has done too much early.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Closer Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the final furlong and one of the genuinely held-up horses finds a clear run to deliver a sustained late challenge.
scenarios.body: Brain Freeze is the most credible closer here with a win and three places from similar Good-going 5f sprints, and Gwen Tennyson showed a recent third at 5f on Good; however, Catterick's flat 5f offers limited room for closers to manufacture significant ground from deep.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Disrupts All Plans
scenarios.trigger: If crowded early running or a poor start scrambles positions, leaving the outcome dependent on which horse recovers best mid-race.
scenarios.body: Mimime and Dunnington Lad, both true hold-up types placed into midfield roles and carrying STYLE_FIT discounts, would need the race to completely dissolve into chaos to reach their best position; even then their limited form bases and out-of-role placement cap their upside.

watchPoints.text: Havin A Flyer's surface switch from Southwell Tapeta to Good turf is entirely unproven (sim-going: 1/15) — if she fails to travel as fluently as usual in the opening furlong, the entire race shape built around her uncontested lead collapses.

Without Flaw has finished 7th twice and 4th recently and has not won since — watch whether Warren Fentiman (3lb claimer) gets a clear run from a prominent position, as any traffic trouble would cost the horse its main tactical advantage.

Brain Freeze carries visor headgear and Connor Beasley's record aboard hold-up types on sharp tracks is worth monitoring — the horse needs a clean passage inside the final furlong on a course where gaps can close quickly against the rail.

Mimime and Dunnington Lad are both shown in midfield but are genuine hold-up horses out of their natural position — if either settles too far back from their mapped spot, they are effectively racing beyond their optimal tactical range and should be discounted accordingly.

Doralee's trainer David & Nicola Barron yard is 0 from 8 in the past 14 days — while Doralee's individual form is solid, a trainer in cold form is a relevant filter if the market shortens her price below her true probability.
